quotes.text: The default Payment Element integration includes a Link prompt in the card form.
Prefilled values are never stored unless the customer completes a Link sign-up.
We only store the prefilled information if the customer takes action and provides consent to create a Link account.
Link supports credit cards, debit cards, and qualified US bank account purchases.
They use the same transaction settlement time and processing behavior as card and bank account payments.

old_evidence.text: the same transaction settlement time and guarantees as card and bank account payments.
Any other 6 digits not listed below

findings: Both captures describe the browser Payment Element: the default card form includes a Link prompt, merchant payment method settings control it, and customers already logged into Link can autofill details originally saved with another business. If the merchant already has the email, pass it via elements.create('payment', {defaultValues: {billingDetails: {email}}}); name and address are optional billing data in the examples. Otherwise, the shopper can enter an email and authenticate or enroll in the Element without integration changes, with an eligible supported payment method for the unsaved-details prompt and customer choice. Old/new raw 9–60 and source 13–28. This is a Link account UI and customer data path, separate from checkout confirmation and payment state.

Both captures distinguish accelerated sign-up, default expanded fields with its own Payment Methods/Link or Connected Accounts settings and customer-country, privacy-law and opt-out qualifications, from the independently disableable Dashboard prefill tool, default when Link is enabled. Same-page detection applies when Stripe customer data has not been supplied programmatically. The guide's prose uses `defaultValue` in that sentence, while the actual Web Elements example uses `defaultValues`. Login receives email for OTP and page information is not stored in that path. Sign-up can prefill email, phone or name, is held temporarily in session memory rather than cookies or local storage and persistence requires customer action and consent to create a Link account. Old/new raw 25–35, 62–91 and source 30–43.

Both captures warn to treat publishable-key-associated sandbox Link accounts as public, use no real user data and authenticate sandbox accounts created with any valid email. Success applies to any other six digits, with 000001 invalid, 000002 expired and 000003 max attempts. Old/new raw 93–106; current source 45–47. Checkout comparison is confined to the matching code outcomes in raw/stripe-checkout-link-2025.md:94–105 and raw/stripe-payments-link-checkout-link-2026-11-07.md:79–91.

Table reflow, quote/comma style, whitespace, an illustration CDN URL and prefill spelling are presentational. The extra custom-checkout before-payment query link at new raw 117 is navigation and supplies no extra workflow authority.

Old raw 108–110 described the same settlement time and guarantees. New raw 108–110 describes the same settlement time and processing behavior for additional funding sources as card and bank payments, continuing automatic support without integration changes. The source omits the distinction, and the revised wording supplies no independent proof of guarantee terms, actual settlement, availability, or changes to payment outcomes.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/payment-element-link, the browser Payment Element defaults to a Link prompt in the card form and exposes merchant control in payment method settings. An already logged-in Link customer can autofill details saved through another business. Stripe recommends passing a previously collected email via defaultValues.billingDetails.email, with optional name and address, or letting the shopper enter email in the form and choose to authenticate or enroll with a supported method. Both old raw lines 9-60 and new raw lines 9-60 preserve these paths. In old raw lines 62-91 and new raw lines 62-91, accelerated sign-up expands enrollment fields by default with country, legal, and opt-out conditions. The distinct prefill tool is default when Link is enabled and separately configurable. Its same-page detection requires customer data not already provided, uses session-local memory, stores no detected page data for returning login and persists new enrollment details only after action and consent. source-stripe-payment-element-link.md lines 13-43 preserve the two routes and local memory but blur the controls and omit eligibility and consent conditions. Old raw lines 93-110 and new raw lines 93-110 document public-like, publishable-key-linked sandbox accounts, no real user data and three fixed OTP exceptions to any other six digits succeeding. The current summary at lines 45-47 needs that precise wording. Authentication, enrollment and documented funding characteristics are distinct from payment confirmation and settlement outcomes.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/payment-element-link, old raw lines 93-110 and new raw lines 93-110 establish two material documentation shifts: the named credit, debit and qualified US bank purchases lose exclusivity and the registration sentence, and the additional-funding comparison replaces guarantees with processing behavior while retaining the same transaction settlement time and automatic support. Preserve both May claims as dated and record the omission alongside the affirmative November registration overview at raw/stripe-payments-payment-methods-pmd-registration-2026-11-07.md lines 5-14, with reciprocal warnings between the route and registration guide. The wording does not determine live domain requirements from omission alone, expand funding eligibility, or prove changes to contract terms, successful payment or funds availability. Table reflow, snippet punctuation and the CDN image change are presentation. The custom checkout before-payment link appearing in new raw lines 112-117 beyond old raw lines 112-116 is navigation. In source-stripe-payment-element-link.md lines 30-47 and the Link concept, qualify the toggles, consent and sandbox OTP independently using old raw lines 62-106 and new raw lines 62-106. Browser Elements defaults and sandbox authentication provide no SDK-version, separate mobile or Checkout surface guarantees, server-confirmation contract or live outcome proof.
